our_argument_summary: WIN-069 claims V13 two-zone topology + aetheric refraction validates Australian road distances (6.2% cross-equatorial RMSE, 10.2% same-hemisphere mean error; AGD66→GDA94 as topology evidence). Our review (verdict Misleading) argues: (1) road excess over geodesic is a terrain-and-circuity property, not topology; (2) 6.2% RMSE expressed in absolute positional terms is ~5 orders of magnitude worse than routine sub-m geodesy on a 4,000 km baseline; (3) AGD66→GDA94 is standard regional→geocentric datum evolution, not topology evidence; (4) V13 parameters (a = π×R_Earth, H(r) fits) are calibrated against globe data, so the "validation" is circular; (5) terrain-based road-network analysis (Giacomin & Levinson 2015 descriptive circuity; OSRM tooling Huber & Rust 2016) outperforms V13 on in-sample road-distance recovery. The c7 state inherits c6 (post-EXP-240 retraction of unsupported sub-1%/single-free-parameter circuity quantifier and the in-sample parity reframe) plus the c6→c7 labeling patch ("in absolute positional terms" added to finding, paired with WIN-057's "relative-error terms (sub-0.01%)" label per ISS-2655).

holes_found.description: Carryover from c6 H1 (open as ISS-1498 in c6; ISS-1498 closed 2026-05-11 via narrow-patch disposition, but the specific phrasing "routinely produces single-digit-percent residuals against observed road distances" still appears in detail_evidence with no inline citation supporting the numeric residual claim). Verified present in current text. A strict cite-checking dome defender could argue: "You retracted sub-1% via EXP-240 but the surviving single-digit-percent quantifier is still uncited; the retraction is incomplete." The argument is operationally defensible (OSRM uses the actual road graph so recovered route distances vs. observed will be single-digit-percent by construction in well-mapped regions), and the surviving parity-reframe sentence does not depend on a specific residual figure. Restated here rather than treated as already-closed because ISS-1498's closure note does not record patching this specific phrase.

stronger_arguments.description: The relative-error framing strengthens the comparison rather than weakening it. Sub-meter geodesic distance on a 4,000 km baseline is a fractional error of ~2.5×10^-7 — roughly 6 orders of magnitude smaller than 6.2%. mm-level GNSS gives ~2.5×10^-10 — 8 orders smaller. sub-mm VLBI gives ~2.5×10^-11 — 9 orders smaller. The "absolute positional terms" qualifier is fully consistent with these relative-error figures, and stating both makes the WIN-057/069 cross-WIN comparison symmetric (WIN-057 says relative-error sub-0.01%; WIN-069 currently says only absolute positional). Mentioning the relative-error parallel pre-empts the most natural dome-defender pivot.

kernel_of_truth.description: The dome model correctly identifies that road distances systematically exceed great-circle (geodesic) distances across transcontinental Australia, and correctly identifies that AGD66 was non-geocentric by design — both are real geographic facts (data/wins.json:069 detail_evidence ¶1 cites Norseman–Ceduna ≈1.07; usq.pressbooks.pub/gpsandgnss/chapter/2-2-australian-datums/ as cited inline). The V13 two-zone topology is a creative attempt to model the road excess by allowing the equatorial ring radius to absorb the residual.
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: Both facts admit standard explanations without dome topology. Road excess is a terrain and network-circuity property documented across every continent (data/wins.json:069 detail_evidence ¶5 cites Giacomin & Levinson 2015 DOI 10.1068/b130131p mean circuities ~1.19 across 51 US MSAs). AGD66→GDA94 is a routine regional→geocentric datum transition every continent performed (cited inline from the usq.pressbooks.pub source above and en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geocentric_Datum_of_Australia_1994). The V13 prediction is calibrated against globe distances (a = π×R_Earth ≈ 20,015 km — quantitatively verified this run, see Lens C). None of the three observations — road excess, 6.2% RMSE, datum shift — discriminates between dome topology and standard terrain-plus-geocentric-geodesy.

advocate_mode.best_defense: A fair-minded dome defender accepting our methodological principles (internal consistency, discriminatory power, no default favoritism) would attack on metric scope: "You concede in WIN-069 that your '5 orders of magnitude worse' comparison is in absolute positional terms. The metric we publish is a relative percent-RMSE on distances (6.2% cross-equatorial, 10.2% same-hemisphere). Compare like with like: when standard geodesy actually predicts road distances, OSRM and circuity literature land in the 5–10% relative-error band on real road networks — not the millimeter band you cite. Your sub-meter / mm-GNSS / sub-mm VLBI numbers are positional capabilities of measurement systems, not of road-distance prediction. The honest comparison on our metric is: V13 same-hemisphere mean error 10.2% in-sample vs. OSRM-circuity baseline ~5–10% in-sample. That is a difference, but it is one factor of two, not five orders of magnitude. By tucking the qualifier into the finding without restating the relative-error case, you let readers conflate measurement positioning capability with distance-prediction capability — exactly the strawman you accuse us of building."
advocate_mode.preemptive_recommendation: Add a single relative-error parallel either in the finding (after the "absolute positional terms" clause) or — preferred — in tldr_evidence/tldr_verdict, making clear that the comparison ALSO holds in relative-distance-error terms (sub-m / 4000 km ≈ 2.5×10^-7 vs. 6.2%, ~6 orders). Separately, the existing in-sample parity sentence in detail_evidence ¶5 ("V13's same-hemisphere mean error is 10.2% with ≥4 free parameters, several times worse than the single-digit-percent in-sample residuals that are routine") already addresses the like-for-like road-distance comparison; promoting that sentence (or a digest of it) into the finding/TLDR would close the surface that the defender exploits. Severity 3 because the rebuttal is structurally coherent and concedes only one labeling slot, but the detail_evidence already contains the right preemption — it just isn't surfaced in the high-visibility fields.

claims_checked: a = π × R_Earth = 20,015 km (disc radius from globe radius)
6.2% RMSE × ~4,000 km baseline = positional error of order "hundreds of km"
"~5 orders of magnitude worse than sub-meter geodesy in absolute positional terms"
quantitative_verification.computations: All computed independently this run via python3. (1) π × 6,371 km = 20,015.09 km — matches the dome's stated disc radius a = 20,015 km to within rounding. (2) 6.2% × 4,000 km = 248 km — confirms the "hundreds of km positional error on transcontinental routes" framing. (3) 248,000 m / 1 m = 2.48×10^5 → log10 = 5.39 — supports "~5 orders of magnitude" against sub-meter. (4) 248,000 m / 1 mm = 2.48×10^8 → log10 = 8.39 — supports "~8 orders" against mm-GNSS. (5) 248,000 m / 0.1 mm = 2.48×10^9 → log10 = 9.39 — supports "~9 orders" against sub-mm VLBI. (6) 248,000 / 1 = 2.48×10^5 — matches "~250,000×" framing. (7) Arc-vs-chord deviation for a 146.6 km segment on R=6378 km computed as L²/(24R²) ≈ 9.4×10^-6 ≈ 0.0022% — the dome's road IS the chord, so the relevant comparison is chord vs. great-circle arc; the road is ~0.002% shorter than the geodesic, i.e. ~180× tighter than the "<0.4%" figure our text uses. The 0.4% bound is generous (not wrong, just very loose). All other numerical claims in the WIN are verified accurate.
quantitative_verification.discrepancies: Only the "<0.4%" figure (and its mirrors in tldr_evidence and tldr_verdict) is quantitatively loose by ~180×. This is c6 H3 / ISS-1500 — restated above as a c7 carryover hole.

deeper_analysis:
This c7 cycle is the first WIN-069-anchored review since c6 (2026-04-23). The finding_length drift (206→235, +14.1%) is entirely accounted for by commit 2d6b2133 (decider self-apply, EXP-603 batch, ISS-2655) inserting " in absolute positional terms" after "5 orders of magnitude worse than sub-meter geodesy", as part of a cross-WIN labeling-consistency patch with WIN-057. The mechanical landing of that patch was confirmed by WIN-057.c7 (queue_id 506, 2026-06-08): all five verify-mode checks pass and explicitly state "WIN-069.finding carries absolute positional terms label". So the textual change is mechanically sound.

What WIN-057.c7 did NOT do is apply WIN-069-specific lenses to the post-patch state. This c7 closes that gap. Lens A (advocate mode) surfaces a genuinely tractable defender pivot: the labeling clause "in absolute positional terms" invites the defender to argue we conceded the comparison metric. The detail_evidence already preempts this (the second paragraph compares "sub-meter accuracy in distance" on a 4,000 km baseline, which is equivalently a relative error of ~2.5×10^-7), but only expanded-view readers see it. The finding and both TLDRs currently lead only with the absolute-positional framing, so a skim-reading defender (or an AI doing the skim) can plant the "they conceded" flag. The fix is small (one parallel relative-error sentence) and surfaces preemption that already exists in detail_evidence — rating defense_survives=3, recommendation minor_edit.

Lens B (cross-WIN consistency) confirms the WIN-027/057/069 cluster is internally consistent at the verdict level (all three Misleading), and the EXP-603 labeling patch made the cluster MORE consistent by giving WIN-057 a relative-error label and WIN-069 an absolute-positional label. The minor asymmetry that WIN-057 carries both labels while WIN-069 only carries one is captured under hole[3].

Lens C (quantitative verification) all-greens the WIN's six headline numbers (disc radius identity, 6.2%-vs-baselines arithmetic, 8/9-order magnitude claims, ~250,000× multiplier). The single quantitative weakness — the "<0.4%" geodesic-deviation figure on the 90-Mile Straight being ~180× looser than the true arc-chord deviation (~0.002%) — is the c6 carryover hole H3 / ISS-1500, restated. This is loose-not-wrong; ISS-1500 was closed 2026-05-11 but the closure note does not record the actual text change, and verification this run confirms the loose figure is still present in detail_evidence, tldr_evidence, and tldr_verdict. Curmudgeon recommends tightening on the next WIN-069 micro-pass; not blocking.

The three minor c6 holes (H1 single-digit-percent citation, H2 "thousands of road pairs" haggle bait, H3 "<0.4%" looseness) are all still present in current text despite their corresponding ISSs (1498/1499/1500) being closed 2026-05-11. Tracker entries for those issues record closure without a text-change closure_note. I'm restating these as c7 carryover holes (severity minor) with unresolved_prior_cycle entries pointing to ISS-1498/1499/1500 so the decider's M3 carry-over enforcement can either (a) verify a patch did land and the text genuinely is correct and these are false carryovers, or (b) escalate them as still-open. Each individual hole is low priority and the verdict stands; the cluster suggests a single sub-200-byte micro-EXP could close all three.

Verdict "Misleading" continues to hold. The TLDR fields and detail_verdict_text accurately summarize the detail content; the only TLDR-level imprecision is the inherited "<0.4%" figure (hole 3).
